chapter: Trumpet teachers and St. Louis heroes
title: Charlie Creath's sound and sharp dress
summary: Thomas praises Charlie Creath's individual trumpet sound and his dapper pongee shirts. Creath worked the riverboats.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Well, Charlie Creath (?) impressed me. Charlie Creath was a tremendous trumpet player.
But, not in the same style as Louis?
Well, I mean what style did Charlie Creath play in?
Yeah, but I mean, yes, Joe. But, I wondered if you could liken him to anybody. Did he sound more like Joe Smith than Louis or did he sound like, he was quite individual.
He sounded like Charlie Creath [SINGS]. And the chicks would run and jump on the boats behind him. He was tremendous.

Tremendous trumpet player and now with sound, he had a trumpet sound. I can't classify people. You know as you grow older, everybody has their own sound. It's an individual thing and he had something to say. And I think really another thing that impressed me was the idea of Creath, Charlie Creath, his dress was so sharp. Stan, (why don't you call him) the poncee shirtsman?
You kidding, 'ain't I sharp.' Handsome cat, you know. Had those pongee shirts.
Oh, he worked boats, of course, yes.
